Identity (mathematics) | In mathematics an identity is an equality relation "A" = "B", such that "A" and "B" contain some variables and "A" and "B" produce the same value as each other regardless of what values (usually numbers) are substituted for the variables.  In other words, "A" = "B" is an identity if "A" and "B" define the same functions.  This means that an "identity" is an "equality" between functions that are differently defined.  For example, ("a" + "b")  =  "a" + 2"ab" + "b" and cos("x") + sin("x") = 1 are identities.  Identities are sometimes indicated by the triple bar symbol ≡ instead of = , the equals sign.
Statement analysis | Statement analysis, also called investigative discourse analysis and scientific content analysis (SCAN), is a technique for analyzing the words people use to try to determine if what they said is accurate.  Proponents claim this technique can be used to detect concealed information, missing information, and whether the information that person has provided is true or false.
